subject: physics
question_text: Name two fundamental areas of physics combined to build a robot.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya IPE Study Material for Jr. Students 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 14 Very Short Answer Question 3 (printed p.143). Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. Chapter 14 is new to the 2026-27 syllabus and no board has examined it, so there is no exam history to cite. The 1 + 1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: mechanics and electromagnetism are confirmed as the two areas needed for a robot's motion and actuation; some study materials print thermodynamics as the second area instead, for heat removal, and that alternative is recorded on this card.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Mechanics
lines: It is the physics behind the forces
and torques needed to move the
steps.why: Mechanics is the physics behind rigid-body motion, so it determines the forces and torques needed to move a robot's limbs and joints.
common_mistakes: Naming mechanics without saying what it supplies — the forces and torques for motion.
Writing 'physics' alone instead of naming mechanics specifically.
steps.memory_tip: Mechanics moves the limbs: forces and torques at each joint.
steps.margin_note: Some study materials name thermodynamics instead, for heat removal — see the note on the next step.

steps.label: Electromagnetism
lines: It is the physics behind the motors
that drive the joints and the
sensors that read the robot's state.
steps.why: Electric motors and most sensors work on electromagnetic principles, so electromagnetism is the second essential area for a robot's motion and sensing. A few study materials print thermodynamics as the second area instead, for the heat removed from motors and circuits — this card follows mechanics plus electromagnetism.
common_mistakes: Naming thermodynamics as the second area. Heat removal matters in a robot, but it does not supply the motion or the sensing.
Naming electromagnetism without saying it supplies the motors and sensors.
steps.memory_tip: Electromagnetism moves it: motors move the joints, sensors read the state.
steps.margin_note: Thermodynamics, for heat removal, is also printed as the second area in some materials.
